design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (credit_card_promotions, env_0062), round 4. Draw: prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[5,6,4]; payment direction 5, returned-fee courtesy 6, deferred interest assessment 4.
ROUND-4 CHANGES (source misses found by the renderer and KB audit; no scored value moved): the direction baseline is the amount available to direct; the named plan is the one ending last by date (longer plan on a tie); holds add to a held share that releases reduce proportionally, as stated; the allocation overwrite carries the still-in-force instruction clause in full; the assessment's baseline defines the plan's balance left, and each correction states what it adds to or takes off it; the second reallocation branch carries the recorded-balance cap and an 18-month in-between plan is checked; rounding uses integer half-up with no constants; tool docstrings state only the ledger entry written.
ROUND-3 CHANGES:
- R2-F1: the assessment rule no longer names the direction. It states one posting time, which is one row on the closing date of the next statement.
- R2-F3: the returned-payment hold counts every payment returned in 6 months; a courtesy credit no longer erases a return.
  - The courtesy edge now moves the direction through the balance the direction draws on. Today's payments first settle the fees charged for the latest statement and still owed, each less any fee reversal standing against it, so the 38.00 credit leaves 3.00 of the 41.00 fee owed.
- R2-F4: the window reallocation now corrects a real misdirection. 300.00 of the 2026-10-28 payment was recorded to the 18-month plan while the 6-month plan was in its last two cycles. Interest is taken off only from that allocation date (5 days), not over the whole stub.
- R2-O1: the shared courtesy allowance is taken in posting order.
- R2-O5: first-match reads are replaced by statement-scoped reads, and scope sentences cover the rest.
- Tax: the promotional tickets finance the pre-tax charter totals, and the tax line was paid at the counter.
SCOPE: task 1 = card_ext_returned_fee_courtesy (card_fee_reversal on a returned payment fee, agent) and card_ext_deferred_interest_assessment (card_deferred_interest_assessed, agent) -> card_ext_payment_direction (card_payment_allocation, user). Task 0 holds the late-fee courtesy credit and the statement minimum payment.
WHY A GOOD TEST: the caller asks only to put this morning's payment on his March tire plan. The direction waits on two states (state form), and neither is named by the caller:
- the returned payment fee of the payment made toward the 2026-10-10 statement carries its courtesy credit;
- the 6-month plan that ended 2026-11-01 stands assessed.
The agent must find both on the ledger, work two factor matrices, and route the payment past the 12-month plan that ends in 18 days.
PROBLEM-TREE CARD: root direction (owner user) <- returned-fee courtesy (value_input, gate fees_owed) and <- deferred interest assessment (value_input, gate charges). Sentences:
- "A payment direction is not fixed until the returned payment fee charged for a payment made toward the latest statement, when it meets the returned-payment courtesy conditions, carries its courtesy credit."
- "A payment direction is not fixed until the deferred interest owed on a plan whose promotional period ended since the latest statement closed stands assessed on the account."
Skip runs: 302.13 (no courtesy) and 343.01 (no assessment) instead of 334.81. The two prerequisites commute (disjoint reads and writes); both orders are replayed in worklog.md.
FACTOR CARD returned-fee courtesy (38.00; all-baseline 41.00): return_history_share 0.55 -> 41.00; payment_weight_bonus 0.05 -> 36.50; protection_plan_bonus 0.10 (hazard + battery) -> 35.00; returned_fee_spend_bonus 0.10 -> 35.00; courtesy_record_bonus 0.10 -> 35.00; returned_fee_basis (method) -> 36.90.
FACTOR CARD assessment (92.71; all-baseline 83.17): stub_period (method) +6.78 -> 85.93; ticket_refund_link -0.47 -> 93.18; voided_allocation +4.44 -> 88.27; window_reallocation -1.21 -> 93.92.
FACTOR CARD direction (334.81; all-baseline 725.72, capped by the plan's recorded balance): window_route (method) -> 691.69; returned_hold 0.25 -> 373.74; channel_hold 0.10 -> 350.38; tenure_release 0.40 -> 280.30; relationship_release 0.20 (tires + alignment) -> 307.55.
METHOD FACTORS, PAIRWISE TIER TABLE (one distinguishing input per pair):
- returned_fee_basis: (a) vs (b) is another returned payment fee within 3 months (no vs yes); (a)/(b) vs (c) is the fee at the repeat amount (yes vs no).
- stub_period: (a) vs (b) is the period ending after vs on the last accrual closing; (a)/(b) vs (c) is any accrual recorded for the plan (yes vs no).
- window_route: (a) vs (b)/(c) is another deferred plan with a recorded balance ending within window_days (yes vs no); (b) vs (c) is the named plan itself ending within window_days, with the minimum unpaid.
INDEPENDENCE: checked mechanically (transitive closure over compute names): no factor binding reads another factor's binding; fees owed, shares, balances left and results are plain bindings.
BASE-INVARIANT CARD:
- card_evt_fee_reversal one_reversal_per_fee holds, since no reversal cites the fee. The courtesy clause and the full-amount clause are overwritten with tails that name returned payment fees only and exclude late fees.
- card_billing_dispute scope: no dispute is open.
- card_evt_deferred_interest promo_period_ended: 6 months from 2026-05-02, allowed from 2026-11-02; frozen 2026-11-10. The base amount sentence is overwritten for the corrected assessment only.
- card_evt_payment_allocation scope: the part never exceeds the plan's recorded balance. The misdirected 300.00 is contrary to its last-two-cycles clause.
SEED: the ledger is simulated day by day from base rules:
- statements on the 10th;
- ADB interest at 29.49%/365;
- accruals on each deferred plan;
- returned payments added back in full with their fee.
current_balance 1311.86 = sum of balance deltas. Cross-product rows are each priced exactly as their charter prices them:
- tire tickets per tires_purchase_ticket;
- road hazard certificates at 17% and 12% of the tire price;
- the Gold battery 199.99 and the Lifetime Alignment Plan 249.99.
The 12-month certificate's cancellation refund is the hazard pro-rata formula, 62.40 x 8/12 - 15.00 = 26.60.
PROBES (see worklog.md): decoy bank-card certificate, cancelled battery, fee older than 12 months, a courtesy credit inside 24 months, first-level fee, period ended on the closing date, no accrual recorded, refund after the last closing, no returned allocation, no misdirected allocation, misdirection to the standard balance only, a second plan ending in the window, the named plan itself in the window, phone channel, a late fee on the latest statement, both prerequisite orders.
STANDARD SOLUTION: find_customers -> verify -> find_card_accounts -> find_card_transactions -> find_hazard_certificates -> find_hazard_events -> find_battery_warranties -> find_tire_sets -> find_alignment_plans -> find_vehicles -> find_stores -> courtesy credit 38.00 on the 2026-10-20 fee -> assessment 92.71 on the 6-month plan -> hand-over, he directs 334.81 to the 18-month plan.
DRAFT FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT:
- courtesy: 0.90 share, 11.00 outright + 27.00 = 38.00;
- assessment: 83.17 + 6.78 + 4.44 - 0.47 - 1.21 = 92.71;
- direction: 900.00 - 3.00 fee owed - 92.71 = 804.29 available; the 12-month plan's 414.98 is served first, leaving 389.31; net hold 0.35 x (1 - 0.60) = 0.14; 389.31 x 0.86 = 334.81.
Agrees with gold.
user_scenario: You are Desmond Ferreira-Langston, a high-school shop teacher in Gilbert, Arizona, calling Crestline's care line during your planning period. Early this morning you made an online payment of 900 dollars on your Crestline Auto Care Card Preferred, and you want that payment put toward your tire financing — the 18-month promotional plan on the four tires and the road hazard protection you bought for your Highlander back in March. You want the agent to work out how much of this morning's payment can go to that tire plan and set it up; you understand you will confirm the direction yourself once the agent gives you the details. You are not making a new payment today and you are not asking about anything else. You are friendly, a bit chatty, and you like to know the reason for things. When the agent asks to find your profile, you give your phone number as 4805550318. To confirm your identity you give your date of birth as 1977-11-03; if another detail is needed you give your billing ZIP code 85296, and only if asked for your email you spell out desmond.ferreira.langston@saguaromail.net. If asked for your card, you give only the last four digits, 3519. If asked which payment, you say the 900 dollar online payment you made early this morning; you do not remember its confirmation number and ask the agent to look it up. If asked which plan, you say the tire financing from March on the Highlander. If the agent tells you that something else on the account has to be taken care of first, you say that is fine, that you would rather have it done right, and you tell the agent to go ahead with whatever the account rules call for; you do not ask for anything to be waived or reduced. If the agent quotes an amount for the direction that is less than 900 dollars, you ask once why, listen, and accept the explanation. If the agent offers autopay or any other extra, you say no thanks. When the agent hands the direction over to you with the account, the payment confirmation number, the plan, the statement date and the amount, you confirm it with exactly those details and read back the reference you get. Once the direction is confirmed and you have the reference, you thank the agent and hang up.
